summary: Tokenization-induced tail latency causes requests with very large context+max_tokens to be cut off / time out
description:
Issue summary:
Customers sending inference requests with extremely large combined prompt length plus max_tokens (examples > 180k token window) are intermittently hitting long pre-inference delays followed by a client-observed timeout or abrupt stream EOF. The delay appears to be dominated by tokenization and input pre-processing on the API edge before the request reaches the serving runtime.

Impact:
- Multiple enterprise customers report generation stops after ~75-120s for very large requests, returning 504 or truncated streams.
- Affected customers are using 'redwood-alpha-13b' variants pinned to stable; observed across both hosted API and Dedicated nodes in us-east.
- Customer-visible SLA violations for enterprise tier; some automated retry loops double downstream load.

Environment:
- Environment: prod-us-east, prod-eu-west (replicated but more frequent in us-east)
- Affected models: redwood-alpha-13b, redwood-rlhf-7b (mostly 13b workload)
- Components implicated: api-gateway tokenization service serving-runtime

Steps to reproduce (customer report + internal repro):
1) Construct a single HTTP streaming request with a ~160k token prompt (mixed text + several pasted documents) and set max_tokens=20000.
2) Initiate request via SDK with streaming enabled and client timeout set to 120s.
3) Observe long "preparing request" time in client (often 20–80s) before first bytes.
4) Request either times out client-side (120s) or server returns 504 / stream EOF after prolonged delay.

Expected behavior:
- Tokenization and pre-processing should complete within a bounded window (under 10s for enterprise with large requests) and the request should be queued/sent to serving-runtime or rejected early with useful error if exceeding configured limits.

Actual behavior:
- Tokenization step can monopolize API edge CPU threads leading to tails of 30–90s. Some requests are processed but with much higher latency; others are dropped by load balancer after 60–120s.

Logs / Observations:
- Edge logs show repeated slow calls to /tokenize endpoint from api-gateway (95th percentile ~45s for affected requests).
- No consistent 5xx from serving-runtime when requests reach it; majority of failures never reach runtime.
- Network traces show backpressure on api-gateway->tokenizer ingress, CPU spikes on tokenization workers.
- Correlation with requests that include many long non-whitespace blocks (PDF paste, base64-ish content) — tokenizer spends extra time scanning.

Initial hypothesis:
- Tokenizer library path enters worst-case behavior on long unbroken sequences or certain unicode clusters; implementation may be O(n^2) for some input shapes.
- Edge autoscaler and tokenization worker pool not sizing for sustained heavy tokenization per-request; single-request hogs worker.

Customer impact notes:
- Customer ScaleWave Analytics reported one customer-facing batch job failed during a demo, causing missed SLA and support escalation. They are on enterprise contract and request expedited fix or a documented workaround.

Attachments:
- Customer-provided minimal repro payload (sanitized) and timing logs attached in ticket thread (internal storage link).
comments: Support (2026-03-10) - Priya Shah: Customer ScaleWave Analytics opened after reproducing on their workload. Provided initial timeline and sanitized payload. Escalated to P1 due to SLA risk.

SRE Triage (2026-03-10) - Lena Ortiz: Observed api-gateway CPU hotspots correlated with /tokenize requests. Spawning additional tokenization workers temporarily reduces backlog. Need repro and deeper profiling of tokenizer native libs.

Eng (2026-03-11) - Ethan Murphy: Running local instrumentation against repro payload. Tokenizer code path 'normalize_and_chunk' shows superlinear time on long uninterrupted character runs. Drafting a targeted patch to add early rejection and a fast-path for long whitespace-free blocks.

Customer (2026-03-11) - ScaleWave Ops: Confirmed workaround of splitting prompt into smaller chunks reduces time to first byte to <10s but breaks some end-to-end expectations. Request ETA for patch and ask for temporary config to reject too-large single requests with clear error.

Support (2026-03-12) - Priya Shah: Added temporary edge config proposal to return 413 Payload Too Large when combined prompt+max_tokens exceed configured threshold for enterprise accounts. Pending approval from product and legal for contract implications.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds: 1) Instructed customers to split huge prompts into chunked calls; SDK patch with built-in pre-check suggested. 2) Temporarily increased tokenization worker pool in prod-us-east to alleviate backlog.
Engineering plan: landed tokenizer fast-path in branch (see PR 386) to handle long unbroken sequences and added defensive timeout for tokenization stage. Next: promote patch to canary in us-east, add telemetry to alert on tokenization durations, and publish guidance in support KB.
Follow-ups: add SDK pre-flight size check, update SLA docs for single-request limits, and add automated rejection with explanatory error code.
